title: Father, Son, and Spirit, Hear
description: Father, Son, and Spirit, Hear in Tonic Solfa to WATCHMAN, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 515. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to WATCHMAN; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, Son, and Spir-it, hear Faith's ef-fec-tual fer-vent prayer; Hear, and our pe-ti-tions seal, Let us now the an-swer feel. Still our fel-low-ship in-crease, Knit us in the bond of peace; Join our new born spi-rits, join Each to each, and all to thine.

lines: Let us now the answer feel.
Knit us in the bond of peace;
Each to each, and all to thine.
Build us in one body up,
Called in one high calling's hope:
One the Spirit whom we claim,
One the faith, and common Lord,
Over, through, and in us all,
One with God, the source of bliss,
Life of all that live below,
Be to us what Adam lost.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to WATCHMAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
